summary: The round-2 major is closed. The BOM now has the C13 mains cord, the cord fact is recorded in the adapter's catalog note with an element14 source, and the BOM also lists the USB Mini-B cable, the 3-pin header the servo plug pushes onto (red in the middle, brown on the outside, as on a standard servo plug), the ball-end driver and real buy links. gnd_common takes the Nano's ground to the jack's minus terminal, so no header pin carries two wires. I recomputed the new routes by hand (servo_pwr 207.6 mm routed, 238.7 mm minimum cut, 250 mm cut; gnd_common 88.8, 102.1 and 110 mm) and the ratings (2.5 of 6 A; burst rise 4.9 K and 1.9 K; ampacity 3.5 and 7 A). Geometry, sweep, insertion and FEA are unchanged from my round-2 probes, and 81 electrical, catalog and access tests pass. What remains are engine follow-ups and documented margins.

findings.issue: The generated packages still give the wrong action words. WIRING.md and the Electrical section of ASSEMBLY.md say 'solder jack -> servo' and 'solder nano -> jack', but both ends are screw terminals or a header; the run notes printed after them say so, so the correct instruction is there. ASSEMBLY.md step 6 (servo) still leaves out the washers, removing the grommets, the top-first insertion from behind and the ball-end driver. DESIGN.md and the BOM have all of these. This is an engine issue in ship.py and wiring_out.py, not this project's design.
findings.fix: In wiring_out.steps, choose the verb per end ('clamp into the screw terminal' for connector items, 'solder to the header' when the run declares a header end). In ship.py, add to each fastener step the matching bom_extra items, the ball-end warnings from hex_keys and the item's insert direction. Add tests.

findings.issue: Nothing checks voltage drop. Checked as AWG 24, the adapter cord drops about 0.42 V at the 2.5 A stall, so the servo would see about 4.5 V, below its 4.8 V minimum, while the report still shows 'servo input 5.0 V' as passing. DESIGN.md now states this, and the effect is harmless here: the rig uses 11 % of stall torque and runs at 0.9 A.
findings.fix: Add an IR-drop term along each feed path at peak current (resistance at 100 C, both conductors, plus connector resistance where catalogued) to the voltage-range check.

findings.issue: tab_z is still unconfirmed (26.5-30.2). At 30.2 the 20 mm horn disc sits 0.5 mm inside the 20.56 mm window with about 0.28 mm to its top and bottom edges, and the arm is 2.5 mm off the wall face. It is clear in every probe, and DESIGN.md now says to measure tab_z before printing.
findings.fix: Measure tab_z on the real servo and catalogue it. Optionally make the window about 1 mm taller (the pilot-hole wall depends on X, not on the window height) to remove the rub risk outright.

findings.issue: The two tab screws next to the cable boss need a ball-end driver. It is documented and now in the BOM as a tool.

Some BOM rows have no buy link or price: the mains cord, the Mini-B cable, the header, the AWG 22 wire, the adapter, the jack and the Nano. The total of $14.86 therefore leaves out most of the electrics, and the adapter alone costs more than that.
findings.fix: Add catalog/prices.json entries (or bom_extra links) for these rows so the BOM total is real.
